detailed_analysis: The fitted band centers (141.1, 196.6, 393.6, 514.4, 636.4 cm-1) match the anatase TiO2 Raman active modes: Eg(~144), Eg(~197), B1g(~399), A1g+B1g(~516), Eg(~639). The dominant Eg mode at 141 cm-1 is very strong (relative intensity 1.0) and narrow (FWHM ~11 cm-1), consistent with well-crystallized anatase; a slight downshift from 144 toward 141 and the narrow width are typical of larger, well-ordered crystallites (nanoscale anatase would blueshift and broaden this band, so this points to bulk/large-grain material). The intensity ordering (141 >> 394 > 514 > 636 > 197) reproduces the canonical anatase pattern. No rutile signature (447/612 cm-1) or 144-absence is seen, so the material is essentially phase-pure anatase. The weak broad hump near 297 cm-1 and the band near 794 cm-1 are not fundamental anatase modes; 297 is likely a weak second-order/combination feature or fit artifact, and 794 (broad, FWHM-railed) is most plausibly a second-order overtone (anatase shows weak features ~796 cm-1, the B1g overtone) rather than a distinct phase. The linear baseline and 0.206 baseline fraction confirm a non-fluorescent crystalline oxide. The persistent bimodal residual on the 141 cm-1 band suggests real asymmetry (Fano-type or anharmonic broadening common in the anatase Eg mode) that a symmetric pseudo-Voigt cannot fully capture. No chemistry (EDX/XRF) was provided, so this is a pattern-only identification, but the full five-band match (positions AND relative intensities) strongly supports anatase over any single-band coincidence.

scientific_claims.claim: The spectrum is identified as anatase TiO2, with the dominant Eg mode at 141.10 +/- 0.03 cm-1 (FWHM 11.4 +/- 0.1 cm-1) and companion bands at 196.6, 393.6, 514.4, and 636.4 cm-1 matching the anatase mode pattern in both position and relative intensity.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: A phase-pure anatase identification with a sharp, only slightly downshifted main Eg band indicates well-crystallized, likely bulk/large-grain material rather than nanoscale anatase; the precise Eg position and width are diagnostic of crystallite size, oxygen stoichiometry, and strain state.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone observed a phase-pure anatase TiO2 with an Eg Raman mode at ~141 cm-1 and FWHM ~11 cm-1, and how do this position and width map to crystallite size and stoichiometry?

model_type: Sum of 7 pseudo-Voigt peaks on a linear baseline (Levenberg-Marquardt least squares); reseeded/retuned peak_1 (~141) and peak_4 (~394) to narrower FWHM + intermediate-high eta, reassigned peak_2 (~197 narrow) and peak_3 (~307 broad hump), FWHM capped at 50 cm-1; flat/linear baseline confirmed (rolling-min baseline area fraction = 0.206, not fluorescence-dominated)
